entries.title: 1 Corinthians 2:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 He declares that his preaching, though it bring not excellency of speech, or of human wisdom, yet consists in the power of God; 6 and so far excels the wisdom of this world, and human sense, that the natural man cannot understand it.

when. Ac 18:1-4 with. 4,13; 1:17; Ex 4:10; Jer 1:6,7; Ro 16:18; 2Co 10:10; 11:6 the testimony. 1:6; Isa 8:20; Ac 20:21; 22:18; 2Th 1:10; 1Ti 1:11; 2Ti 1:8 1Jo 4:14; 5:11-13; Re 1:2,9; 19:10

entries.title: 1 Corinthians 2:14
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
the natural man.[Psuchikos ,] the animal man, one who lives in a natural state, and under the influence of his animal passions; for [psuche ] means the inferior and sensual part of man, in opposition to the [nous ] understanding, or [pneuma ,] the spirit.
